title: Real-time data for AI agents: sources for research, prospecting and news
summary: How to give AI agents real-time data for research, leads and news: the live web through Firecrawl, plus data providers and indexes in Firecrawl Alexandria.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR**


- **Real-time data for AI agents is information the agent fetches while it works** , from the live web, data providers and search indexes, instead of from a model's training data, which stops at a cutoff date.
- **Firecrawl gives agents all three through one account.**[Firecrawl /search](https://www.firecrawl.dev/search) and[Firecrawl /scrape](https://www.firecrawl.dev/scrape) read the live web.[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/) adds data providers such as Apollo, SEC EDGAR, Benzinga and Particle, plus Firecrawl's own Government & Legal, Research and Developer indexes.
- **It works in ChatGPT, Claude and any MCP client.** Connect Firecrawl once and ask for research, leads or news in plain language. Developers get the same tools through the API, SDKs and CLI.


---


## What is real-time data for AI agents?


Real-time data for AI agents is information an agent pulls at the moment it needs it, such as a page read a minute ago, a filing posted this morning or a funding round from last week. It replaces guesses from the model's training snapshot with facts that carry a date and a source the agent can cite.


That data comes from three kinds of sources:


- **The live web.** Search results and pages, read on demand.
- **Data providers.** Structured records, such as people, companies, filings and news headlines, from the businesses and public bodies that publish them.
- **Specialized indexes.** Search indexes built for one field, such as law, scientific papers or developer documentation.


Firecrawl's white paper,[AI's Search-Bar Problem](https://www.firecrawl.dev/whitepapers/ais-search-bar-problem) , describes how the layers fit together:


> The live web is the starting point: today's prices, this morning's job postings, the injury report that dropped an hour ago. Behind it sits the material serious work depends on.


Each source answers a different kind of question:


Source How current it is What the agent gets back Best for


Model training data Stops at the model's cutoff date Recall with no source Reasoning, drafting, summarizing


Live web search and scraping Current when the call runs Pages as Markdown with their URL Open questions, company sites, press coverage


Data providers As current as the provider's own data Typed fields, such as title, headcount or filing date Leads, financials, structured lookups


Specialized indexes Refreshed on the index's schedule Ranked passages from primary sources Law, research papers, code questions


Our guide to[training data vs. retrieved data vs. live web data](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/training-vs-retrieved-vs-live-web-data) covers when each layer wins on its own.


## Why do AI agents need real-time data?


An AI agent's model knows only what it saw in training, so anything that changed after its cutoff is invisible to it. Prices, job titles, funding, laws and headlines all change. Without a fresh source, the agent fills the gap with an old fact and states it as confidently as a current one.


Teams running agents see this in production. In a[VB Pulse survey of 101 enterprises](https://venturebeat.com/data/57-of-enterprises-have-watched-ai-agents-be-confidently-wrong-the-fix-is-an-agentic-context-layer-but-who-has-one) published in July 2026, **57%** had traced a confident but wrong agent answer to missing or inconsistent context in the previous six months. A[Harris Poll for Collibra](https://www.collibra.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/new-survey-from-collibra-by-the-harris-poll-finds-72-of-tech-decision-makers-feel-ai-initiatives) found that **87%** of data and AI decision-makers have their teams regularly re-check that the context their agents use is accurate and current.


Developers writing about agents make the same point. One[DEV Community post](https://dev.to/jamilxt/your-ai-agent-depends-on-more-than-its-model-the-microsoft-365-outage-is-a-warning-1lbd) from November 2026 argues that an agent that can't reach its source should say so, rather than "quietly answer from stale context."


[Credal](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/credal-firecrawl-ai-agents) , which runs AI agents for enterprise customers, uses Firecrawl for exactly this:


> We run production agent workflows where the model needs either fresh external context or non-standard data without ETL. Our customers need their agents to reference today's facts or pull from their customer-facing support docs without building a custom integration.


*[Jack Fischer](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jackfischer11/) , Co-Founder and CTO,[Credal](https://www.credal.ai/)*


## How does Firecrawl Alexandria give AI agents real-time data?


Firecrawl Alexandria is Firecrawl's library of data providers and specialized indexes, which AI agents call through one Firecrawl account. The agent describes what it needs, gets matching tools back for free, reads each tool's inputs and price, then runs it and receives structured records with their source.


When Firecrawl tested it across 845 tasks with the same model and prompts, AI agents using Firecrawl Alexandria scored **21% higher on answer quality** than agents with built-in web tools, judged blind. The[Firecrawl Alexandria launch post](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-alexandria-series-b) covers that test, and our[explainer on data connectors](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/data-connectors) covers how agents reach third-party data in general.

The sections below map the three most common agent jobs (research, lead generation and news monitoring) to the tools that serve them.


## Which real-time data sources fit research jobs?


Research jobs need sources an agent can quote. Firecrawl /search answers open questions from the live web, with a time filter to keep results recent. Firecrawl Alexandria adds the Research Index for papers, the Government & Legal Index for law, the Developer Index for code questions and SEC EDGAR for company filings.


Research job Firecrawl tool


Find recent coverage, product pages or announcements on a topic Firecrawl /search with a time filter, then Firecrawl /scrape on the pages worth reading


Find the papers behind a claim[Research Index](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/firecrawl-research-index)` search`


Find the statute, regulation or ordinance behind a rule[Government & Legal Index](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/firecrawl-gov-index)` search`


Answer a question about a library, API or error message[Developer Index](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/firecrawl-developer-index)` search`


Read a public company's profile and latest filings[SEC EDGAR](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/sec-gov)` filings/companies_get`


See what people are searching for right now[Trends](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/firecrawl-trends)` trends/trending_now`


Hand off a multi-step research question[Firecrawl /agent](https://www.firecrawl.dev/agent)


The source an agent can reach changes the answer it gives. In Firecrawl's[Legal Information Retrieval Benchmark](https://www.firecrawl.dev/benchmarks/legal-retrieval) of 581 legal research requests, the Government & Legal Index put the official document first **76.2%** of the time, against **47.8%** for an agent working from memory, and had it in the top ten results on **96.6%** of requests.


Filings, papers, court opinions and city codes often arrive as PDFs. Firecrawl /scrape reads them in the same call and returns Markdown, tables included. The engine underneath,[Fire-PDF](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/fire-pdf-launch) , is built in Rust and is one of the fastest PDF parsers in the world. It runs on[pdf-inspector](https://github.com/firecrawl/pdf-inspector) , Firecrawl's open-source PDF library and a developer favorite with more than 20,000 GitHub stars, which parsed a 200-PDF[benchmark set](https://github.com/firecrawl/pdf-inspector#benchmark) in 0.47 seconds.


Our post on the[Government & Legal Index](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/government-legal-index) shows the legal side in more depth, and[agentic search](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/agentic-search) covers how agents search the web at reasoning time.


## Which real-time data sources fit lead generation?


Lead generation needs current records about people and companies. Firecrawl Alexandria's people and company providers return titles, firmographics and contacts as structured fields, jobs providers show who is hiring, and Firecrawl /scrape reads a prospect's own site for the details a database doesn't hold.


Lead generation job Firecrawl tool


Find people by title at target companies[Apollo](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/apollo)` people/search`


Look up a company's firmographics from its domain[FullEnrich](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/fullenrich)` companies/lookup`


Find companies hiring for a role your product serves[TheirStack](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/theirstack)` jobs/search`


Browse startups by Y Combinator batch[Y Combinator](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/ycombinator-com)` companies/batches`


List local businesses in a city[Maps](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/firecrawl-maps)` businesses/search`


Read a prospect's pricing, product or careers page Firecrawl /scrape


Some providers, such as Apollo and FullEnrich, ask an admin on your Firecrawl team to accept their terms once before the first call. Our[B2B prospecting guide](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/b2b-prospecting) walks through the full process from account list to first line.


## Which real-time data sources fit news monitoring?


News monitoring needs a way to pull recent coverage on demand and a way to hear about changes without asking. Firecrawl /search returns news results and time-filtered web results, Firecrawl Alexandria adds news and podcast providers, and[Firecrawl /monitor](https://www.firecrawl.dev/monitor) sends alerts when something changes.


News job Firecrawl tool


Pull this week's coverage of a company or topic Firecrawl /search limited to the past week, or set to return news results


Track market-moving headlines on US-listed companies[Benzinga](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/benzinga)` news/search`


Search news about a company or topic[Akta](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/akta)` news/search`


Find podcast episodes that mention a company or person[Particle](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/particle)` podcasts/episodes/search`


See which searches are trending today[Trends](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/firecrawl-trends)` trends/trending_now`


Get an alert when a page changes or a result matching your goal appears Firecrawl /monitor, with page, website or web-wide search targets


Firecrawl /monitor checks on a schedule you set and notifies you by webhook, email or Slack, so an agent can react to news instead of polling for it.


## How do you connect real-time data to ChatGPT, Claude or your own agent?


Firecrawl connects to ChatGPT through a plugin, to Claude through a connector, and to any other AI agent through the Firecrawl MCP server. Each one signs in to your Firecrawl account, so there is no API key to paste. Every tool in this post is available once you connect, except that a few providers, such as Apollo and FullEnrich, need an admin on your Firecrawl team to accept their terms once first.


- **ChatGPT:** open **Plugins** , search for **Firecrawl** , select **Install** and sign in.
- **Claude:** add the Firecrawl connector from the connector directory, sign in, then turn it on from the **+** menu.
- **Claude Code:** run` claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` , then finish signing in from` /mcp` .
- **Codex:** install the Firecrawl plugin in the Codex app, or run` codex mcp add firecrawl --url https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` and then` codex mcp login firecrawl` .
- **Cursor or any MCP client with a JSON config:** add` https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` as a server named` firecrawl` .


[Add Firecrawl to ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl)


[Add Firecrawl to Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/firecrawl)


### What prompts can you paste in?


Each prompt names Firecrawl and the tools it should use, and asks for a source and date on every fact.


**Research:**


```text
Use Firecrawl to research how US states regulate AI chatbots in customer service.
Search the Firecrawl Government & Legal Index for the statutes and bills, and use
Firecrawl search (past 3 months) for recent coverage. Give me a table of state,
rule, status and effective date, with the source link and publication date for
every row.
```


**Lead generation:**


```text
Use Firecrawl Alexandria to find 10 US fintech companies hiring AI engineers in
the past 14 days (TheirStack). For each company, add its size and HQ from
FullEnrich and the heads of engineering from Apollo. Show the job post link for
each row. Don't look up contact details yet.
```


**News monitoring:**


```text
Use Firecrawl to brief me on Nvidia from the past 7 days: news search, Benzinga
headlines and analyst ratings, and podcast mentions from Particle. Merge stories
about the same event into one line, keep the earliest source, and flag anything
without a clear publication date.
```


### How do developers call the same tools?


Developers can call every tool in this post from the[Python, Node.js, Go and Rust SDKs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/overview) , the[REST API](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/alexandria) or the[Firecrawl CLI](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/cli) . API and SDK callers add` sources: \["alexandria"\]` to Firecrawl /search to find Firecrawl Alexandria tools, and ask for prices with` includeCosts: true` on the MCP server or` --include-costs` in the CLI. This Python example pulls the past week's results from the live web, then searches the Research Index through Firecrawl Alexandria:


```text
import   os
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl


firecrawl   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  os.environ[  "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"  ])


# Web results from the past week, straight from the live web
recent   =   firecrawl  .  search  (  "AI agent startups funding"  , tbs  =  "qdr:w"  , limit  =  5  )
for   item   in   recent  .  web   or   []  :
print  (item.title, item.url)


# Research papers from the Firecrawl Research Index, through Firecrawl Alexandria
papers   =   firecrawl  .  scrape  (
alexandria  =  {
"provider"  :   "firecrawl-research-index"  ,
"capability"  :   "search"  ,
"options"  : {  "query"  :   "evaluating retrieval for LLM agents"  ,   "k"  :   3  },
},
)
for   paper   in   papers  .  alexandria  [  0  ].  data  [  "results"  ]:
print  (paper[  "title"  ])
```


## How much does real-time data for AI agents cost with Firecrawl?


Finding a Firecrawl Alexandria tool is free, and each tool shows its price in Firecrawl credits before it runs. Searches of the Government & Legal Index and the Research Index cost nothing. The free plan includes 1,000 Firecrawl credits a month with no card, and paid plans start at $19 a month, billed monthly.


Firecrawl Alexandria needs a signed-in Firecrawl account or a Firecrawl API key. Firecrawl /search, Firecrawl /scrape and the Government & Legal, Research and Developer indexes also work without a key, within a daily limit per IP address, so you can try them before signing up. Each provider page on[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers) lists its tools and their prices, and[pricing](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) has the plan details.


Firecrawl is used by teams at 67% of the Fortune 100, and any team that needs a security review can start with the[enterprise page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/enterprise) and the[security docs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/enterprise) .
